newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes edge up amid lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes edge up amid lackluster trade.

text.p: Crude oil prices on the U.S. West Coast edged higher Monday in quiet trade, with traders continuing to evaluate their supply needs for next month.

No new sales of regional benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were reported Monday. The crude has declined steadily relative to U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) for nearly three months after peaking in early March at an 80 cent discount to WTI.
BP America sold a cargo to Texaco Transport and Trading at a discount of $1.75 on May 23.
Buyers expected the next cargo to sell at $1.90-$2.00 off July WTI.
Outright prices for ANS ranged $19.30/19.50 a barrel Monday, tracking higher spot and futures markets.
Differentials for heavier valley crudes were lower following a fall in posted prices Friday.
